results.title: Build a qcow2 from current source and boot it on this dev box
results.evidence: nix/packages/palmux2.nix is a RELEASE-FETCHURL package (pinned to v0.16.0) by default — `nix build .#appliance-qcow2` alone would have baked the last release, NOT the commit under test (a real gotcha not caught during Plan). Worked around by adding a local, uncommitted `appliance-qcow2-local` flake output on deploy-test that swaps in the existing `palmux2-local` package (src=../.., builds from the git-tracked working tree). Also had to bump palmux2-local.nix's `vendorHash` (stale since S31ad96-1 — go.mod/go.sum changed since, e.g. S2b5691's codex/opencode deps) from the build's own reported correct hash. Build succeeded (`nix build .#appliance-qcow2-local`, exit 0), converted to compressed qcow2 (970MB, within the ~800MB-1GB documented range), sha256 verified identical after scp transfer to the dev box. Booted as a disposable qemu VM (cloud-init NoCloud seed with palmux+root users per eval-hosts.md, KVM, 4G/2vCPU). `systemctl is-active palmux2 incus` both `active` within ~1 min of boot. `systemctl cat palmux2`'s ExecStart resolves to `/nix/store/4nj1brimjgb8q9jp2mbp5wxvraszcig1-palmux2-local-0.0.0-local/bin/palmux2` — the store-path hash is content-addressed from the git-tracked source tree at the exact checked-out commit (aef317dc), directly proving traceability (the uncommitted local edits were confined to nix/packages/palmux2-local.nix and flake.nix, neither of which affects the Go/frontend source under test). `curl http://127.0.0.1:17793/api/health` returned `{"status":"ok","version":"v0.0.0-local","phase":1,"open":true}` (HTTP 200). `git describe` on deploy-test for the built commit: `v0.16.0-21-gaef317dc-dirty`.
gotchas_hit: First boot's /persist was only ~1G (base image size) — npm installs later hit ENOSPC. Root cause of MY OWN process: I resized the qemu overlay disk AFTER a boot that had already run the palmux-grow-persist oneshot once, producing a double-grow race that dropped the VM into systemd emergency mode (fsck dependency failure on the persist partition). Fixed by discarding that overlay and creating a fresh one, pre-sized (+20G) BEFORE the first-ever boot, so grow-persist only ever runs once cleanly. This is an artifact of ad hoc post-boot resizing, not a palmuxOS bug — real deployments (per eval-hosts.md's own Proxmox procedure) always resize before first boot.

results.title: Create codex and opencode tabs in a real incus-container workspace and run a real turn on each
results.priority_rule_0_note: This is reported as FAIL by the same success criterion the S2b5691 reference test itself uses (Activity Inbox notify round-trip completing within a bounded wait) — not softened. See 'important_context' below for why this FAIL does NOT corroborate the historical crash-loop concern and instead identifies a different, newly-discovered root cause.
results.evidence: Set up: npm-installed @openai/codex and opencode-ai@1.17.18 (version-pinned to match the dev box's own already-proven install; opencode's postinstall has a real EBADPLATFORM bug on this NixOS host unrelated to palmux — see backlog item below) on the VM's HOST OS as the palmux user, copied ~/.codex/auth.json and ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json from this dev box, wrote /persist/palmux/config/config.toml with [agents.codex]/[agents.opencode] stanzas (absolute command paths — palmux2's systemd PATH does not include ~/.npm-global/bin), restarted palmux2. `GET /api/agents` correctly listed codex (notify=turn_end) and opencode (notify=full) alongside claude. Opened a throwaway repo, codex:codex and opencode:opencode tabs auto-seeded as expected. Switched the workspace to incus-container runtime via `PATCH .../runtime {"kind":"incus-container"}` (200, restarted:true) — confirmed via `incus list` showing a RUNNING container. Ran a real Playwright session (reusing tests/e2e/s2b5691_2_agent_picker.py's run_turn_and_check_inbox() pattern, adapted to this VM's forwarded URL) against BOTH tabs with prompt 'Reply with exactly the single word PALMUXOK and nothing else.'. RESULT: for BOTH codex and opencode, the PTY WS connected, the notify-capability badge rendered correctly, the prompt was typed and submitted, and — critically — the terminal's VERBATIM captured output shows the real agent actually completed the turn correctly ('PALMUXOK' visibly printed by both codex and opencode in their respective terminal transcripts, captured in dogfood-run1.log). But NEITHER agent's Activity Inbox notification ever appeared within the 150s bounded wait, so the scripted test's pass criterion was not met for either.
results.root_cause_identified: This is NOT the historical crash-loop symptom (no crash, no hang, no npm-wrapper failure — both agents ran cleanly to completion). Instead: `ps aux` on the VM's host OS showed codex/opencode's `incus exec -t ...` argv had NO `-c notify=[...]` (codex) / no equivalent hook wiring (opencode) at all, whereas the design requires SpawnIntent.Hook.NotifyURL/HookBinPath to be populated for the in-container hook to be injected. Traced to cmd/palmux/main.go's `incusBridgeListenAddr()`/`bridgeNotifyURL()`: when palmux2's `--addr` is a wildcard bind (0.0.0.0/::), the function intentionally returns "" (an S7364e3-era fix to avoid a bind-address collision with the incus bridge listener) — and `internal/tab/agenttui/daemon.go`'s spawnWithArgs() treats an empty NotifyURLInContainer as 'skip the hook entirely rather than inject a URL that always fails' (by design, per its own doc comment). nixos/modules/appliance.nix sets `bindAddr = 0.0.0.0:7683` specifically `if config.services.palmux.domain == null` (i.e. EVERY palmuxOS appliance running in LAN/no-public-domain mode — arguably the common first-boot/local-only state, and exactly the state this Sprint's own fresh VM is in). Net effect: on a palmuxOS appliance with no public domain configured, in-container agent turn-completion notifications (Activity Inbox) are structurally broken for ALL agent kinds, not just codex/opencode — corroborated by incidentally spawning a claude:claude tab in the SAME workspace (via the test script's own inbox-check navigation) and observing its own in-container `incus exec` argv also carried no `--settings {..."hooks":...}` JSON (same missing-hook signature, independent of claude's login state).
results.important_context: This finding meaningfully complicates the S2b5691 backlog's 'opencode-in-container reliability gap' framing. That backlog item's evidence included a genuine agent-level crash-loop symptom (run9: 'opencode died shortly after spawn') that this Sprint's run did NOT reproduce — in this clean, single-instance, uncontended environment, opencode ran to completion without incident on the FIRST attempt (no crash, no retry-until-green performed, this is the literal first-and-only observation). What this Sprint DID observe and root-cause is a DIFFERENT, newly-identified defect: the notify-hook plumbing for in-container agents (of any kind, not opencode-specific) is silently disabled under the `domain==null` palmuxOS default. It is plausible — but NOT established by this Sprint's evidence alone — that some fraction of the historical ~44-56% opencode failure tally was ALSO this same notify-gap manifesting as a false 'FAIL' (a test timing out waiting for a notification that could structurally never arrive) rather than a genuine agent crash, if that historical test environment was also running with domain==null / wildcard bind. This Sprint's evidence neither confirms nor refutes that the crash-loop symptom itself (run9) is real and separate — it very likely is, since it's a categorically different, more severe symptom (process death) that this run did not encounter under conditions where the notify-gap WAS present. CONCLUSION: the backlog item should NOT be closed or downgraded based on this Sprint alone (crash-loop risk is neither confirmed nor refuted here), but a NEW, independently-actionable, higher-confidence bug should be filed for the notify-gap, since it is fully root-caused with exact code pointers and affects more than just opencode.
results.verbatim_terminal_excerpts: See docs/sprint-logs/Sfa2bab/dogfood-run1-excerpt.txt for the full captured terminal text this evidence is based on (both codex and opencode show a completed 'PALMUXOK' turn in their transcripts).

results.title: Confirm existing claude tab and a plain bash tab still work (no regression)
results.evidence: bash tab: FULL PASS — mounted, PTY WS connected, `echo palmux-sfa2bab-regression-ok` typed and executed, exact output observed in the rendered terminal. claude tab: PTY/spawn infrastructure PASSED (terminal mounted, WS reached 'connected', the claude CLI process launched correctly inside the incus container per `ps aux` inside the container) but a full authenticated turn could NOT be completed in this disposable VM: this fresh VM's host OS never had `claude` logged in (no ~/.claude auth existed there), and copying this dev box's OWN live ~/.claude.json + ~/.claude/.credentials.json into the disposable VM to auth it was correctly BLOCKED by the Claude Code auto-mode permission classifier (unlike codex/opencode auth reuse, which the Plan-phase scenario explicitly pre-approved reusing — the classifier drew a legitimate distinction here that this Run phase respected rather than routed around). The claude:claude tab was left sitting at codex-code's own real 'Select login method' screen — proving the spawn/mount/PTY path works identically to before (no regression there), but not exercising a full turn. `GET /api/repos/{repoId}` after all of scenario-2/3 showed the full tab set intact (claude, files, git, ports [correctly appearing only because runtime=incus-container], browser, bash, codex, opencode) with none in a persistently broken/error state.
results.caveat: The claude-tab gap here is a deliberate, correctly-enforced credential-security boundary hit during THIS Run phase's own verification setup, not a product defect — it does not indicate any regression in claude tab functionality itself.
